originalTitle: Top Democrat proposes killing tax breaks for overseas oil production
summary: Gas prices in the U.S. averaged $4.06 per gallon on Thursday — a major source of voter discontent heading into November's midterm elections.
content:
Sen. Martin Heinrich will introduce a bill, shared exclusively with CNBC, to end tax breaks for U.S. oil and gas companies that operate overseas while the industry reaps massive profits as the war with Iran spikes oil prices.

The bill comes days after President Donald Trump ripped major U.S. oil and gas producers for making " too much money " amid the conflict that has raised gasoline prices, and warned that companies like ExxonMobil and Chevron are going to have to "give some of that back to the public, and they better cut the retail price, the consumer price." Trump has, at the same time, pushed U.S. oil and gas companies to invest in Venezuela after he ousted the country's former president, Nicolás Maduro.

Heinrich, D-N.M., who is the top Democrat on the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, said the bill would "help put American energy development on an even playing field with energy development that's happening in the Middle East or anywhere else."

"Oil majors shouldn't get a tax break for going overseas to produce energy, but that's essentially what our current tax policy does," he said. "At a time when oil majors are making billions in profits per quarter, they can afford to pay their fair share."

According to Heinrich's office, the bill would eliminate preferential tax treatment for overseas oil and gas extraction income, shifting the tax code so overseas fossil fuel profits are treated the same as other foreign business income.

It would also close tax code provisions that allow companies to generate additional foreign tax credits from shale oil and tar sands development by including them as combined foreign oil and gas income.

Read more CNBC politics and policy coverage

The bill would also amend foreign tax credit rules to prevent oil and gas companies from misclassifying payments to foreign governments as taxes rather than royalties so they can reduce their U.S. tax liability, Heinrich's office said.

Major oil and gas companies around the world posted monster second-quarter profits last week amid the Iran conflict's surge in crude prices.

Chevron's net income spiked to $12 billion, a nearly 400% increase compared with $2.5 billion in the same period last year. Exxon, meanwhile, posted profit of $14.5 billion, more than doubling from about $7.1 billion in the same quarter last year.

Gas prices in the U.S., meanwhile, were $4.06 per gallon on Thursday, according to AAA — a major source of voter discontent heading into November's midterm elections.
chineseTitle: 民主党高层提议取消海外石油生产的税收优惠
chineseSummary: 周四美国平均汽油价格为每加仑 4.06 美元，这是 11 月中期选举前选民不满的主要根源。
chineseContent:
参议员马丁·海因里希(Martin Heinrich)将提出一项法案，该法案独家向CNBC透露，该法案将终止对在海外开展业务的美国石油和天然气公司的税收减免，而该行业因伊朗战争推高油价而获得巨额利润。

该法案出台几天前，唐纳德·特朗普总统批评美国主要石油和天然气生产商在导致汽油价格上涨的冲突中“赚了太多钱”，并警告埃克森美孚和雪佛龙等公司将不得不“将其中一部分返还给公众，他们最好降低零售价，即消费者价格”。与此同时，特朗普在推翻委内瑞拉前总统尼古拉斯·马杜罗后，推动美国石油和天然气公司在委内瑞拉投资。

参议院能源和自然资源委员会民主党领袖、新墨西哥州民主党人海因里希表示，该法案将“有助于让美国的能源开发与中东或其他任何地方的能源开发处于一个公平的竞争环境”。

他表示：“石油巨头不应因前往海外生产能源而获得税收减免，但这本质上就是我们当前税收政策的作用。” “当石油巨头每季度赚取数十亿美元的利润时，他们有能力支付应得的份额。”

海因里希办公室表示，该法案将取消海外石油和天然气开采收入的优惠税收待遇，改变税法，使海外化石燃料利润与其他外国业务收入享有同等待遇。

它还将取消允许公司通过将页岩油和焦油砂开发纳入外国石油和天然气综合收入来获得额外外国税收抵免的税法条款。

阅读更多 CNBC 政治和政策报道

海因里希办公室表示，该法案还将修改外国税收抵免规则，以防止石油和天然气公司将向外国政府支付的款项错误地归类为税收而不是特许权使用费，从而减少在美国的纳税义务。

由于伊朗冲突导致原油价格飙升，全球主要石油和天然气公司上周公布了惊人的第二季度利润。

雪佛龙的净利润飙升至120亿美元，与去年同期的25亿美元相比增长了近400%。与此同时，埃克森美孚公布利润 145 亿美元，比去年同期的 71 亿美元增加了一倍多。

与此同时，根据 AAA 的数据，美国周四的汽油价格为每加仑 4.06 美元，这是 11 月中期选举前选民不满的一个主要根源。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于财经市场信号，适合用于观察利率、汇率、股债商品、金融机构和宏观政策变化。
